sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, Histaklut Penimit 9

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, Histaklut Penimit 9:1
items.html:
It explains the order of the emanation of the Partzuf Galgalta of AK, and it contains three matters: 1. That it is the first expansion of the light of Ein Sof for the coupling by striking. 2. That the coupling is made upon the screen of phase four, which raises reflected light up to Keter, and there emerged the ten Sefirot of the Rosh, the ten Sefirot of the Toch, and the ten Sefirot of the Sof. 3. The reason Malchut can expand from the Peh downward into the ten Sefirot of the Guf is that all the light that the lower one causes to the upper one, the lower one attains as well; and since Malchut, together with her reflected light, caused the ten Sefirot of the Rosh to be attained, she too therefore acquired ten Sefirot.

The ten Sefirot of the Rosh, of Galgalta, of AK
And we shall first explain the Partzuf Galgalta of AK, which is the first Partzuf in the world of AK, and is the beginning of everything. You already know that Ein Sof expands to the coupling by striking upon the screen that is in the vessel of Malchut, whereupon the reflected light, repelled from the vessel of Malchut, ascends and clothes the four phases of direct light up to the stature of Keter. You also know that this clothing of the ten Sefirot of direct light in the ten Sefirot of reflected light is called the ten Sefirot of the Rosh, meaning roots of vessels, for the clothing of the reflected light from below upward suffices only to attain the light in the Partzuf, but not to clothe it in actuality, as above.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, Histaklut Penimit 9:2
items.html:
The reason for the expansion of Malchut of the Rosh into ten Sefirot is that every degree that causes light to the one above it attains it as well
And it is known that the law in the upper worlds is that every degree that causes an addition of light to the degree above it, all of that addition of light returns and is bestowed as well upon that same degree that caused its appearance. And therefore, since Malchut did not receive the light that belonged to her, and returned it to its place — that is, it became the reflected light that turned into a garment upon the upper light, by which she attained the upper light in the Rosh, as above, for without this reflected light the upper light would not have been attained there at all — it necessarily follows that the whole of that stature of the ten Sefirot of the Rosh, which she caused there, returns and expands as well within the vessel of Malchut herself. Similar to what is said of ZA, that “three came out of one, one stands in three,” so too here in Malchut: out of the nine that came out of one, one stands in the nine. And this and that are called Guf.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, Histaklut Penimit 9:3
items.html:
The ten Sefirot of the Toch, of Galgalta, of AK
And therefore the reflected light returns to shine within the vessel of Malchut, in a manner that expands her to the five phases KHB TM, and the ten Sefirot of direct light of the Rosh shine forth as well and expand into the ten Sefirot of Malchut, that is, as far as the Malchut within her, called Tabur. And these five phases of the aforesaid expansion of Malchut are what become complete vessels for the clothing of the upper light in the Partzuf, and therefore they are called Guf, as is known (and see Inner Light, Part 3, Chapter 2, item 3, and Chapter 3, item 1).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, Histaklut Penimit 9:4
items.html:
The ten Sefirot of the Sof, of Galgalta, of AK
And from the Tabur downward, the upper light can no longer expand there, because of the restriction and the screen within it; and therefore there is nothing there but the illumination of reflected light without direct light, which has no power to expand, and therefore they conclude the Partzuf, as above (Chapter 7, item 2). And thus the RTS [Rosh-Toch-Sof] of the first Partzuf of AK, called the Partzuf Galgalta, have been explained.
